significance: Temperance Lloyd, Susanna Edwards, and Mary Trembles were hanged at Exeter on 25 August 1682, following prosecution originating in Bideford, Devon — the last judicial witch executions in England, preceding the formal repeal of the Witchcraft Acts by fifty-four years.
source_method: Bideford Borough Records; Devon Record Office; contemporary pamphlet A True and Impartial Relation (1682); analyzed in Hutton, The Witch (2017); Levack, The Witch-Hunt in Early Modern Europe (2006)
